key_insight: Manufacturing-oriented simplification of a generatively designed UAV tail boom reduced mass by 4% and print time by 20% while eliminating supports.
engineering_relevance: Symmetric arms, self-supporting geometry, and uniform cross-sections can improve FFF manufacturability without changing the assessed load-bearing adequacy under the studied quasi-static loads.
method: Compare topology-following and FFF-oriented variants of the same generative design.
Evaluate both using linear static and buckling FEA under identical loads.
Print scaled simplified prototypes in two bounding infill configurations and load-test them.
evidence_signal: Simplification increased peak FEA stress by 31%, but it remained below 2% of the assumed ultimate tensile strength; predicted stress concentrations qualitatively matched observed fracture locations.
watch_item: Scaled prototype tests and quasi-static FEA do not establish full-scale flight durability or fatigue performance.
paper_title: Post-processing strategies for generative design outcomes in a UAV tail boom
